title: Reserve-to-Burst Conversion Operator and Customer SQ Debrief
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Goal: Prototype and validate a Reserve->Burst conversion operator that lets enterprise customers convert reserved GPU minutes into transferable burst credits under controlled rules, and capture answers for customer's Security Questionnaire (SQ) related to reserved/burst flows.

Context: Customers buying Dedicated capacity ask for more flexibility when demand is spiky. Current reserved commitments are rigid; customers request a mechanism to credit unused reserved capacity as burstable credits (region-bound or cross-region) they can spend during peak windows or transfer to other teams. This ticket ties packaging experiments (pricing, conversion ratios, limits) with enterprise SQ deliverables so sales/legal can respond to procurement.

Scope:
- Define operator semantics: conversion ratios, expiry, region constraints, preemption handling, and accounting reconciliation.
- Pricing experiments: floor price for converted credits, surcharge for cross-region conversion, and refund/true-up rules.
- Prototype billing and usage pipeline changes to represent credits in the invoice.
- Draft SQ responses for ~12 reserved/burst-related questions (KMS, logging, data residency, audit trails, tenant isolation).
- Run a controlled pilot with 2 anchor accounts for 8 weeks to observe economics and operational edge cases.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc agreed by PM/Eng/Sales and uploaded to Confluence
Conversion operator implemented behind feature flag in staging and passes integration tests
Billing emits 'converted_burst_credit' line items with correct attribution for pilot accounts
SQ draft completed and reviewed by Security & Legal with sign-off comments resolved
Pilot run plan scheduled and two anchor customers enrolled with signed pilot terms
metrics: Pilot adoption: 2 customers onboarded within 2 weeks
Utilization delta: % of converted credits consumed within 30 days
Unit economics: realized avg $/GPU-minute for converted credits vs baseline reserved rate
SLA incidents: count of availability or preemption-related customer-impacting events during pilot
Customer NPS change for participating customers after 8 weeks
rollout_plan: Week 0-2: Finalize operator rules, pricing tiers, and SQ draft
Week 3-4: Implement operator and accounting pipeline; internal dogfood
Week 5: Security & Legal review; update SQ answers based on infra changes
Week 6-13: Execute 8-week pilot with anchor accounts; daily monitoring for first 2 weeks then weekly
Week 14: Synthesize results, recommended pricing adjustments, and go/no-go decision for broader beta
risks_mitigations: Risk: Conversion credits could be gamed to avoid committed spend -> Mitigation: enforce conversion windows, caps, and per-account conversion budgets
Risk: Billing reconciliation complexity increases -> Mitigation: add dedicated billing line items and reconciliation job + test harness
Risk: Cross-region data residency/legal concerns -> Mitigation: default converted credits to same region unless customer explicitly opts-in with SQ confirmation
Risk: SLA mismatches when burst uses preemptible pool -> Mitigation: surface clear latency/availability tiers and require customer acceptance in pilot terms
comments: 2025-01-12 - Sofia Martinez: Initial sketch shared in #pm-pricing. Sales asked specifically if credits can be transferred across teams under the same org. Action: add org-transfer constraints.

2025-01-18 - Liam Chen: Met with Priya and Noah. Kernel-level preemption semantics will require a 'lowest-latency' vs 'best-effort' routing decision for converted credits. Eng estimate 5pt for core operator + 3pt for billing hooks.
2025-01-22 - Elena Ruiz: Billing prefers immutable line items for converted credits to avoid downstream ambiguity. We should include credit_id and original_reservation_id on invoice rows.
notes_for_sales: Pilot terms include a clear description of how converted credits expire (default 90 days) and a repayment true-up if preemption causes excess non-delivery. Sales must collect a signed opt-in for cross-region conversions.
security_sq_highlights: We answered the customer's top SQ asks: (1) Converted credits are accounted per-tenant and represented in logs with credit_id; (2) Keys used for billing metadata are stored in customer KMS when customer requests; (3) Audit trail retained for 1 year by default and available to customers on request; (4) Cross-region transfers require explicit org-level consent and legal approval.
next_steps: Finalize conversion rules doc, land billing PR, iterate SQ draft with Marcus, schedule pilot kickoff meeting with two anchor customers (ACME Labs, NovaAI).
